character_action: ayan sits on floor opening a cardboard box of belongings
ayan pulls a yellowed sealed envelope from the box
ayan looks at the envelope with his name in fathers handwriting
dialogue: You never said you wrote me anything.

character_action: ayan holds an old photo of him and his father
dialogue: I was always too busy, Baba. Always next week.

character_action: ayan walks slowly through the empty house touching the wall
ayans hand touches fathers reading glasses on a table
ayan looks at the empty worn armchair
dialogue: It still smells like you in here.

character_action: ayan sits in the armchair and closes his eyes

location: quiet park bench under a tree
character_action: ayan sits alone on the bench
ayans trembling hands open the letter
ayans eyes fill with tears one tear falls
ayan reads listening to fathers words
dialogue: My son. If you are reading this, I am already gone.

character_action: ayan a faint sad smile through tears
dialogue: I was never angry that you were busy. I was proud.

character_action: ayan stands alone at fathers grave holding the letter
ayan looks down at the grave peaceful
dialogue: I will, Baba. Every Sunday. I promise.

character_action: ayans hand places a single flower on the grave
ayan walks away lighter as the sun rises
empty bench a single bird lands on it
